# Hosted API retention and deletion

**Audience:** Support  
**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Status:** Published baseline  
**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Contract-specific terms override this general guidance.

## Support-facing rule

| Data class | Default or commitment |
|---|---|
| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |
| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |
| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |
| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |
| Stored data covered by a verified deletion request | Redwood completes deletion from Redwood-managed systems within 30 days of verification. |

Support must not describe the 30-day deletion statement as proof of backup erasure or tenant-termination cleanup. The available baseline evidence does not establish those behaviors.

## Explicit unknowns

- Whether tenant termination automatically starts a tenant-wide erasure workflow.
- Whether any backup or snapshot may contain Hosted API customer data, and the maximum time until such copies are irrecoverable.
- Whether a deletion confirmation includes backup purge evidence.
- Whether region pinning covers backups, disaster-recovery replicas, and all control-plane metadata.
- Whether legal holds or contract-specific exceptions alter deletion timing.
- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window; this policy does not infer it from request-log retention.

## Validation before answering a customer

1. Confirm the deployment is Hosted API and identify any contract-specific retention or residency terms.
2. Confirm whether debug payload logging is enabled for the organization.
3. For deletion, verify the request and identify each targeted data class; open the approved deletion workflow.
4. Escalate questions about backups, tenant termination, certificates, legal holds, or cross-region copies to Security/Privacy and SRE. Do not promise a completion window until written evidence covers the requested scope.
5. Cite the applicable source and record the customer-specific answer in the support ticket.

Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?\\n\\n1) Are customer request/response payloads stored at rest? If so, where (region/country) by default and can we request EU-only storage?\\n2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and model artifacts?\\n3) After we terminate a tenant or request erasure, what is the timeline for purging primary stores and backups?\\n4) Do backups/snapshots replicate cross-region? If so, what is the maximum retention on backups?\\n5) What controls exist for key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for deletion events?\\n\\nI attached our short questionnaire (crestline-sq.pdf) with the same fields. We need a short written response to include in the packet by COB Tuesday.\\n\\nThanks,\\nEmma Lopez\\nSecurity & Compliance\\nCrestline Health\\n\\nAttachment: crestline-sq.pdf (application/pdf)\",\n    \"From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>\\nCc: \\nDate: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire\\n\\nTeam \\u2014 forwarding Crestline's three-page SQ. They need short, precise answers for their board packet (deadline Tue COB). I drafted a proposal below but want confirmation on retention numbers and the phrasing around backups + purge timelines before I send.\\n\\nMain points to confirm:\\n- Default store region for hosted API (our standard tenancy mapping)\\n- Defaults for request logs vs embeddings vs model artifacts (we have flexibility for enterprise contracts)\\n- Wipe timeline for primary vs backups (we guarantee purge of primary within X days; full backup scrub may take longer)\\n- Language around KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys\\n\\nI attached an internal data-residency-matrix and a suggested doc (crestline_answers_v1.docx). Please reply with any edits.\\n\\nThanks,\\nOlga\\nHead of Solutions - CSM Escalations\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nAttachments: crestline-sq.pdf, data-residency-matrix.xlsx, crestline_answers_v1.docx\\n\\nOn Sat, 30 May 2026 at 09:12, Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health> wrote:\\n> Hi Olga,\\n> \\n> We're finalizing our vendor security questionnaire for the Crestline June board packet and have a handful of specific items on data geography, default retention, and deletion timelines for hosted APIs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?\\n> \\n> [snip]\",\n    \"From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:24:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire\\n\\nOlga \\u2014 draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.\\n\\n1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self\\u2011serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign\\u2011up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).\\n\\n2) Default retention windows (hosted API)\\n- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.\\n- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.\\n- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.\\n- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine\\u2011tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.\\n\\n3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines\\n- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.\\n- Backups / long\\u2011term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross\\u2011region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.\\n\\n4) Backups & cross\\u2011region replication\\n- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU\\u2011only custody we ensure backups remain in\\u2011region; cross\\u2011region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.\\n- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.\\n\\n5) Key management & auditability\\n- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer\\u2011managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.\\n- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Logs include the user, timestamp, object id, and operation status.\\n\\nNotes on evidence: I attached the small residency matrix and architecture diagram if they want an appendix entry. Suggest we offer Crestline the EU tenancy addendum and a 30\\u2011day primary purge / 90\\u2011day backup scrub cadence in writing; that should be acceptable for their board.\\n\\nIf that reads OK, Olga, happy for you to send to Emma.\\n\\n\\u2014 Karthik\\nDirector, Infrastructure Product\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nAttachment: redwood-hosted-arch.pdf\\n\\nOn Sat, 30 May 2026 at 10:02, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:\\n> Team \\u2014 forwarding Crestline's three\\u2011page SQ.\\n> [snip]\",\n    \"From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health>, security@crestline.health\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire\\n\\nHi Emma \\u2014 thanks for the note and the SQ. Please find our short answers below; I\\u2019ve attached a one\\u2011page summary and the draft responses for inclusion in your packet. If your board needs tighter timelines, we can add the EU tenancy addendum and a CMK option to the order form.\\n\\nSummary answers (for packet)\\n\\u2022 Storage location: Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy\\u2019s primary region. Self\\u2011serve accounts default to the nearest regional cluster (US by default); EU\\u2011only tenancy pinning is available under enterprise contract.\\n\\u2022 Default retention: Request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default (configurable to 90/365 for enterprise). Embeddings retained 14 days by default (can be reduced to 7 days). Model snapshots retained until deleted; rolling snapshot retention default 30 days.\\n\\u2022 Erasure timelines: Primary data purge within 30 days after a verified erasure request or tenant termination. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days; we provide a deletion attestation on completion.\\n\\u2022 Backups & replication: Backups may replicate to a secondary region for DR depending on SLA; for EU\\u2011only contracts cross\\u2011region replication is disabled. Max default backup retention 90 days (extendable by agreement).\\n\\u2022 KMS & audit: Encryption at rest via cloud KMS by default; enterprise customers may use customer\\u2011managed keys or HSMs. Deletion/erasure events are logged in the audit trail (365\\u2011day retention) and can be surfaced in the console or delivered as an export for enterprise customers.\\n\\nAttachments: crestline_answers_v1.docx (draft answers), data-residency-matrix.xlsx, redwood-hosted-arch.pdf\\n\\nNext steps: If that looks good I\\u2019ll send a formal addendum for EU tenancy pinning and CMK options. Otherwise send any edits and we\\u2019ll update the doc.\\n\\nBest,\\nOlga Petrov\\nHead of Solutions - CSM Escalations\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nOn Mon, 1 Jun 2026 at 11:24, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:\\n> Olga \\u2014 draft answers and rationale below.\\n> [snip]\"\n  ],\n  \"original_location\": \"gmail/olga_petrov/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3\"\n}",

    "From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Subject: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Hi Olga,

We're finalizing our vendor security questionnaire for the Crestline June board packet and have a handful of specific items on data geography, default retention, and deletion timelines for hosted APIs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?

1) Are customer request/response payloads stored at rest? If so, where (region/country) by default and can we request EU-only storage?
2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and model artifacts?
3) After we terminate a tenant or request erasure, what is the timeline for purging primary stores and backups?
4) Do backups/snapshots replicate cross-region? If so, what is the maximum retention on backups?
5) What controls exist for key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for deletion events?

I attached our short questionnaire (crestline-sq.pdf) with the same fields. We need a short written response to include in the packet by COB Tuesday.

Thanks,
Emma Lopez
Security & Compliance
Crestline Health

> Hi Olga,

>

    "From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Olga — draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.

1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self‑serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign‑up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.
- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.
- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.
- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine‑tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.

3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines
- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.
- Backups / long‑term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross‑region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.

4) Backups & cross‑region replication
- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU‑only custody we ensure backups remain in‑region; cross‑region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.

5) Key management & auditability
- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer‑managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.
- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Logs include the user, timestamp, object id, and operation status.

Notes on evidence: I attached the small residency matrix and architecture diagram if they want an appendix entry. Suggest we offer Crestline the EU tenancy addendum and a 30‑day primary purge / 90‑day backup scrub cadence in writing; that should be acceptable for their board.

If that reads OK, Olga, happy for you to send to Emma.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Product
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-arch.pdf

    "From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the SQ. Please find our short answers below; I’ve attached a one‑page summary and the draft responses for inclusion in your packet. If your board needs tighter timelines, we can add the EU tenancy addendum and a CMK option to the order form.

Summary answers (for packet)
• Storage location: Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy’s primary region. Self‑serve accounts default to the nearest regional cluster (US by default); EU‑only tenancy pinning is available under enterprise contract.
• Default retention: Request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default (configurable to 90/365 for enterprise). Embeddings retained 14 days by default (can be reduced to 7 days). Model snapshots retained until deleted; rolling snapshot retention default 30 days.
• Erasure timelines: Primary data purge within 30 days after a verified erasure request or tenant termination. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days; we provide a deletion attestation on completion.
• Backups & replication: Backups may replicate to a secondary region for DR depending on SLA; for EU‑only contracts cross‑region replication is disabled. Max default backup retention 90 days (extendable by agreement).

    "id": "dsid_c7f6ff2dcf674dd784e7f65c738d0724",

    "title": "Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook\",\n  \"space\": \"customer-success-and-support\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Raman\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"customer-success\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Morales\",\n    \"Priya Nair\",\n    \"Ethan Cole\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"decommission\",\n    \"data-retention\",\n    \"privacy\",\n    \"compliance\",\n    \"playbook\",\n    \"audit\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/private-network-firewall-peering-checklist-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/erase-certification-guidelines-2025\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"body\": \"Summary:\\nThis playbook defines the operational process, verification steps, and evidence collection required to safely decommission a tenant and produce a Data Erasure Certification for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), Account Security leads, and the Privacy Compliance team.\\n\\nScope:\\n- Applies to all Dedicated and Private tenants (reserved capacity or VPC/on-prem) where a customer requests a full tenant decommission and verified data purge.\\n- Excludes transient test tenants created under internal dev projects.\\n- Covers: configuration metadata, KV caches, embedding indices, logs and telemetry tied to tenant IDs, backups/snapshots, and any customer-managed on-prem artifacts we control.\\n\\nGoals:\\n- Ensure data belonging to a tenant is irrecoverably deleted from all Redwood-managed storage within agreed SLA windows.\\n- Produce a signed Data Erasure Certification (PDF) including verification artifacts suitable for customer audit.\\n- Provide a clear rollback and exception path if deletion interferes with legal holds, active billing disputes, or regulatory constraints.\\n\\nPrerequisites and gating checks (Pre-decommission):\\n1) Confirm formal request: must come from the customer\\u2019s authorized admin contact or a signed CSM request form. Attach request to ticket.\\n2) Confirm account state: Tenant must be quiesced for at least 48 hours unless an accelerated erase is explicitly authorized by Legal.\\n3) Verify no active legal holds or retention policies: Check Legal/Evidence mailbox and related JIRA signals.\\n4) Snapshot list: Enumerate all active snapshots, backups, and object storage buckets that contain tenant data.\\n5) Billing & contracts: Finance must sign off that invoicing and reconciliations are complete, or place a hold if a dispute exists.\\n\\nRoles and responsibilities:\\n- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): owner of the decommission process, customer comms, and final handoff of the certification.\\n- SRE / Infra Owner: executes deletion commands, validates low-level storage and KV cache removal, updates runbook evidence.\\n- Privacy & Compliance: reviews evidence, prepares certification language, and signs final PDF.\\n- Account Security Lead: verifies no remaining credentials, SSH keys, certificates, or cross-tenant links.\\n- Finance: confirms final billing state.\\n\\nHigh-level decommission checklist (stepwise):\\n1) Prepare: Create a decommission incident ticket (PREFIX: DECOM-{tenant_id}) and add all owners and reviewers. Attach customer request and any hold flags.\\n2) Quiesce: Disable API keys, revoke incoming webhooks, and switch routing policy to reject new traffic. Record timestamps.\\n3) Export minimal retention artefacts (if requested): generate requested audit logs and export them to a customer-managed bucket; document the export SHA256.\\n4) Snapshot verification: Ensure latest snapshot is stored in immutable archive (if contractually required). Note location and checksum.\\n5) Delete operational artifacts (order matters):\\n   a) Revoke and purge tenant IAM roles and tokens.\\n   b) Remove routing and DNS entries.\\n   c) Stop and delete serving instances (record instance IDs).\\n   d) Wipe KV caches and in-memory stores with secure-delete commands.\\n   e) Delete embedding indices and associated vector DB partitions.\\n   f) Remove object storage buckets and blobs.\\n   g) Delete logs and telemetry for tenant IDs (respecting retention law exceptions).\\n6) Cease backups: ensure backup jobs no longer include tenant and delete retained backup files.\\n7) Final storage sweep: run storage-level compliance scan to find orphaned objects or references.\\n8) Evidence collection: collect command outputs, checksums, S3 / object delete receipts, and storage listings that show 404/NotFound.\\n9) Generate Draft Certification: Privacy prepares draft certification with attached evidence links.\\n10) Sign-off: Legal/Privacy and Finance must approve. Once approved, deliver signed PDF to customer via secure channel and close the decommission ticket.\\n\\nCommands and verification examples (examples - replace with tenant values):\\n- Revoke API keys (CLI): redwood-cli tenants revoke-keys --tenant-id tenant-123 --force\\n- KV cache wipe (runbook snippet): curl -X POST https://kv.internal.redwood/delete-namespace -d '{\\\"tenant\\\":\\\"tenant-123\\\",\\\"mode\\\":\\\"secure\\\"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'\\n- Object store delete + verification (bash):\\n  aws s3 rm s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 --recursive && aws s3 ls s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 || echo \\\"Bucket not found\\\"\\n- Snapshot checksum (example): sha256sum tenant-123-snapshot-20260101.tar.gz > snapshot.sha256\\n\\nEvidence packaging requirements:\\n- Include: ticket export, customer request, command stdout logs (with timestamps), storage deletion receipts, backup job logs, checksum files, and the pre-decommission inventory.\\n- Redact: Do not include PII of Redwood employees in delivered artifacts. Replace internal ticket IDs with redacted tokens when necessary.\\n- Evidence TTL: Internal evidence must be retained in the audited evidence bucket for 2 years (Compliance mandate).\\n\\nVerification checklist (to be ticked in ticket):\\n- [ ] Customer request attached and validated against admin contact.\\n- [ ] Quiesce actions completed and timestamped.\\n- [ ] All API keys and webhooks revoked.\\n- [ ] Embedding indices removed and index count = 0.\\n- [ ] Object storage bucket returns NotFound.\\n- [ ] Backups and snapshots removed or archived as per contract.\\n- [ ] KV cache namespace removed and confirmed.\\n- [ ] Logs trimmed or removed respecting legal holds.\\n- [ ] Privacy & Legal sign-off obtained.\\n- [ ] Signed Data Erasure Certification produced and delivered.\\n\\nRollback and exceptions:\\n- Legal Hold: If a legal hold is identified mid-process, immediately pause deletion steps and notify Legal and the customer. Rehydrate any removed snapshots from immutable archive if possible.\\n- Accidental deletion: If accidental deletion is detected within the retention window, follow the Incident Recovery Runbook (link in related_pages) and escalate to SRE Lead and CTO on-call.\\n- Customer Revocation: Customer may revoke the decommission within the quiesce window if approved; in that case, restore routing and reactivate keys following the Tenant Reactivation checklist.\\n\\nCommunication templates (summary snippets to use in ticket and email):\\n- Initial acknowledgement to customer: \\\"We have received your decommission request. The tenant has been scheduled for quiesce on {date}. Expected completion: {date + X business days}. We will provide a Data Erasure Certification when the process completes.\\\"\\n- Final delivery message: \\\"Attached is your Data Erasure Certification for tenant {tenant_id}. This confirms Redwood-managed artifacts have been erased per the contract. Contact your CSM with any audit questions.\\\"\\n\\nAudit and certification content (what we include in the PDF):\\n- Statement of scope (tenant id, dates, artifacts included/excluded).\\n- Listing of deleted artifact types and counts (buckets deleted, indices removed, instances terminated).\\n- Verification artifacts (checksums, deletion receipts, ticket references).\\n- Signatures: Privacy & Compliance lead + CSE.\\n- Optional: a notarized stamp if requested and pre-approved by Legal (adds 3-7 business days).\\n\\nOperational metrics and SLAs for decommission requests:\\n- Standard FIFO SLA: 10 business days from validated request to certified completion.\\n- Accelerated SLA: 48\\u201396 hours (requires signed acceleration waiver from customer and Legal approval).\\n- Verification SLA: Privacy has 5 business days to review and sign evidence once uploaded.\\n\\nAutomation and tools:\\n- Decommission Orchestrator (internal service): Use the decommission orchestration UI for walk-through steps and to collect structured evidence. If the orchestrator is unavailable, follow the manual runbook steps above.\\n- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/decom/tenant-{tenant_id}/{ticket_id}/\\n- Template generator: internal tool that assembles evidence links into the draft certification.\\n\\nPost-decommission monitoring (30 days):\\n- Watch for retroactive billing anomalies or customer follow-ups. Set a 30-day ticket cooling period where CSE monitors any reappearance of tenant artifacts.\\n- Run a weekly orphan-object scan for the tenant id for 4 weeks post-deletion and archive results into the ticket.\\n\\nAppendices:\\nA) Example minimal Data Erasure Certification language (copy into PDF generator):\\n\\\"Redwood Inference certifies that, as of {date}, Redwood-managed storage and runtime artifacts associated with tenant {tenant_id} were deleted and validated in accordance with the contract and Redwood internal data retention policies. Evidence artifacts are appended/linked in this certification. Signed: {PrivacyLead}, {CSEName}.\\\"\\n\\nB) Quick checklist for small tenants (one-liner):\\n1) Verify request -> 2) Revoke keys -> 3) Delete bucket -> 4) Remove indices -> 5) Deliver certification.\\n\\nC) Emergency contacts:\\n- Customer Success Incident Pager: +1-555-0123 (internal)\\n- Privacy & Compliance Slack: #privacy-compliance (tag @privacy-lead)\\n- SRE On-call: see internal roster or PagerDuty schedule\\n\\nChange log:\\n- 2026-01-12: Playbook created by Aisha Raman.\\n- 2026-01-25: Added accelerated SLA flow and notarization note (review by Legal).\\n- 2026-02-10: Clarified evidence TTL and added orphan-object weekly-scan requirement (reviewers: Diego Morales, Priya Nair).\\n\\nRelated references and links:\\n- Tenant quiesce runbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/scheduled-tenant-quiesce-and-safe-failback-playbook-2026\\n- Data residency & retention policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/policy-2025\\n- Incident recovery runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/incident-recovery-2025\\n\\nOwner and contact:\\n- Playbook owner: Aisha Raman (CSE Lead) - aisha.r@redwood.ai\\n- Privacy reviewer: Priya Nair - priya.n@redwood.ai\\n- SRE liaison: Diego Morales - diego.m@redwood.ai\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_c7f6ff2dcf674dd784e7f65c738d0724\"\n}",

document.title: Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook
document.content:
{
  "title": "Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook",
  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Aisha Raman",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-01-12",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Morales",
    "Priya Nair",
    "Ethan Cole"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "decommission",
    "data-retention",
    "privacy",
    "compliance",
    "playbook",
    "audit"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/private-network-firewall-peering-checklist-2026",
    "/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/erase-certification-guidelines-2025"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "body": "Summary:
This playbook defines the operational process, verification steps, and evidence collection required to safely decommission a tenant and produce a Data Erasure Certification for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), Account Security leads, and the Privacy Compliance team.

Scope:
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private tenants (reserved capacity or VPC/on-prem) where a customer requests a full tenant decommission and verified data purge.
- Excludes transient test tenants created under internal dev projects.
- Covers: configuration metadata, KV caches, embedding indices, logs and telemetry tied to tenant IDs, backups/snapshots, and any customer-managed on-prem artifacts we control.

Goals:
- Ensure data belonging to a tenant is irrecoverably deleted from all Redwood-managed storage within agreed SLA windows.
- Produce a signed Data Erasure Certification (PDF) including verification artifacts suitable for customer audit.
- Provide a clear rollback and exception path if deletion interferes with legal holds, active billing disputes, or regulatory constraints.

Prerequisites and gating checks (Pre-decommission):
1) Confirm formal request: must come from the customer’s authorized admin contact or a signed CSM request form. Attach request to ticket.
2) Confirm account state: Tenant must be quiesced for at least 48 hours unless an accelerated erase is explicitly authorized by Legal.
3) Verify no active legal holds or retention policies: Check Legal/Evidence mailbox and related JIRA signals.
4) Snapshot list: Enumerate all active snapshots, backups, and object storage buckets that contain tenant data.
5) Billing & contracts: Finance must sign off that invoicing and reconciliations are complete, or place a hold if a dispute exists.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): owner of the decommission process, customer comms, and final handoff of the certification.
- SRE / Infra Owner: executes deletion commands, validates low-level storage and KV cache removal, updates runbook evidence.
- Privacy & Compliance: reviews evidence, prepares certification language, and signs final PDF.
- Account Security Lead: verifies no remaining credentials, SSH keys, certificates, or cross-tenant links.
- Finance: confirms final billing state.

High-level decommission checklist (stepwise):
1) Prepare: Create a decommission incident ticket (PREFIX: DECOM-{tenant_id}) and add all owners and reviewers. Attach customer request and any hold flags.
2) Quiesce: Disable API keys, revoke incoming webhooks, and switch routing policy to reject new traffic. Record timestamps.
3) Export minimal retention artefacts (if requested): generate requested audit logs and export them to a customer-managed bucket; document the export SHA256.
4) Snapshot verification: Ensure latest snapshot is stored in immutable archive (if contractually required). Note location and checksum.
5) Delete operational artifacts (order matters):
   a) Revoke and purge tenant IAM roles and tokens.
   b) Remove routing and DNS entries.
   c) Stop and delete serving instances (record instance IDs).
   d) Wipe KV caches and in-memory stores with secure-delete commands.
   e) Delete embedding indices and associated vector DB partitions.
   f) Remove object storage buckets and blobs.
   g) Delete logs and telemetry for tenant IDs (respecting retention law exceptions).
6) Cease backups: ensure backup jobs no longer include tenant and delete retained backup files.
7) Final storage sweep: run storage-level compliance scan to find orphaned objects or references.
8) Evidence collection: collect command outputs, checksums, S3 / object delete receipts, and storage listings that show 404/NotFound.
9) Generate Draft Certification: Privacy prepares draft certification with attached evidence links.
10) Sign-off: Legal/Privacy and Finance must approve. Once approved, deliver signed PDF to customer via secure channel and close the decommission ticket.

Commands and verification examples (examples - replace with tenant values):
- Revoke API keys (CLI): redwood-cli tenants revoke-keys --tenant-id tenant-123 --force
- KV cache wipe (runbook snippet): curl -X POST https://kv.internal.redwood/delete-namespace -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123","mode":"secure"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'
- Object store delete + verification (bash):
  aws s3 rm s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 --recursive && aws s3 ls s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 || echo "Bucket not found"
- Snapshot checksum (example): sha256sum tenant-123-snapshot-20260101.tar.gz > snapshot.sha256

Evidence packaging requirements:
- Include: ticket export, customer request, command stdout logs (with timestamps), storage deletion receipts, backup job logs, checksum files, and the pre-decommission inventory.
- Redact: Do not include PII of Redwood employees in delivered artifacts. Replace internal ticket IDs with redacted tokens when necessary.
- Evidence TTL: Internal evidence must be retained in the audited evidence bucket for 2 years (Compliance mandate).

Verification checklist (to be ticked in ticket):
- [ ] Customer request attached and validated against admin contact.
- [ ] Quiesce actions completed and timestamped.
- [ ] All API keys and webhooks revoked.
- [ ] Embedding indices removed and index count = 0.
- [ ] Object storage bucket returns NotFound.
- [ ] Backups and snapshots removed or archived as per contract.
- [ ] KV cache namespace removed and confirmed.
- [ ] Logs trimmed or removed respecting legal holds.
- [ ] Privacy & Legal sign-off obtained.
- [ ] Signed Data Erasure Certification produced and delivered.

Rollback and exceptions:
- Legal Hold: If a legal hold is identified mid-process, immediately pause deletion steps and notify Legal and the customer. Rehydrate any removed snapshots from immutable archive if possible.
- Accidental deletion: If accidental deletion is detected within the retention window, follow the Incident Recovery Runbook (link in related_pages) and escalate to SRE Lead and CTO on-call.
- Customer Revocation: Customer may revoke the decommission within the quiesce window if approved; in that case, restore routing and reactivate keys following the Tenant Reactivation checklist.

Communication templates (summary snippets to use in ticket and email):
- Initial acknowledgement to customer: "We have received your decommission request. The tenant has been scheduled for quiesce on {date}. Expected completion: {date + X business days}. We will provide a Data Erasure Certification when the process completes."
- Final delivery message: "Attached is your Data Erasure Certification for tenant {tenant_id}. This confirms Redwood-managed artifacts have been erased per the contract. Contact your CSM with any audit questions."

Audit and certification content (what we include in the PDF):
- Statement of scope (tenant id, dates, artifacts included/excluded).
- Listing of deleted artifact types and counts (buckets deleted, indices removed, instances terminated).
- Verification artifacts (checksums, deletion receipts, ticket references).
- Signatures: Privacy & Compliance lead + CSE.
- Optional: a notarized stamp if requested and pre-approved by Legal (adds 3-7 business days).

Operational metrics and SLAs for decommission requests:
- Standard FIFO SLA: 10 business days from validated request to certified completion.
- Accelerated SLA: 48–96 hours (requires signed acceleration waiver from customer and Legal approval).
- Verification SLA: Privacy has 5 business days to review and sign evidence once uploaded.

Automation and tools:
- Decommission Orchestrator (internal service): Use the decommission orchestration UI for walk-through steps and to collect structured evidence. If the orchestrator is unavailable, follow the manual runbook steps above.
- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/decom/tenant-{tenant_id}/{ticket_id}/
- Template generator: internal tool that assembles evidence links into the draft certification.

Post-decommission monitoring (30 days):
- Watch for retroactive billing anomalies or customer follow-ups. Set a 30-day ticket cooling period where CSE monitors any reappearance of tenant artifacts.
- Run a weekly orphan-object scan for the tenant id for 4 weeks post-deletion and archive results into the ticket.

Appendices:
A) Example minimal Data Erasure Certification language (copy into PDF generator):
"Redwood Inference certifies that, as of {date}, Redwood-managed storage and runtime artifacts associated with tenant {tenant_id} were deleted and validated in accordance with the contract and Redwood internal data retention policies. Evidence artifacts are appended/linked in this certification. Signed: {PrivacyLead}, {CSEName}."

B) Quick checklist for small tenants (one-liner):
1) Verify request -> 2) Revoke keys -> 3) Delete bucket -> 4) Remove indices -> 5) Deliver certification.

C) Emergency contacts:
- Customer Success Incident Pager: +1-555-0123 (internal)
- Privacy & Compliance Slack: #privacy-compliance (tag @privacy-lead)
- SRE On-call: see internal roster or PagerDuty schedule

Change log:
- 2026-01-12: Playbook created by Aisha Raman.
- 2026-01-25: Added accelerated SLA flow and notarization note (review by Legal).
- 2026-02-10: Clarified evidence TTL and added orphan-object weekly-scan requirement (reviewers: Diego Morales, Priya Nair).

Related references and links:
- Tenant quiesce runbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/scheduled-tenant-quiesce-and-safe-failback-playbook-2026
- Data residency & retention policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/policy-2025
- Incident recovery runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/incident-recovery-2025

Owner and contact:
- Playbook owner: Aisha Raman (CSE Lead) - aisha.r@redwood.ai
- Privacy reviewer: Priya Nair - priya.n@redwood.ai
- SRE liaison: Diego Morales - diego.m@redwood.ai

  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],

}

    "title": "Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)\",\n  \"space\": \"security-and-compliance\",\n  \"author\": \"Miles Thornton\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"security\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-07\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-12\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Mina Haddad\",\n    \"Victor Alvarez\",\n    \"Simran Kaur\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"security\",\n    \"reliability\",\n    \"failover\",\n    \"data-residency\",\n    \"routing\",\n    \"audit-logging\",\n    \"enterprise\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis document defines **security boundaries that must be preserved during regional failover** for Redwood Inference (Hosted API and Dedicated). It specifies:\\n- How **data residency constraints** restrict routing/failover.\\n- **Audit logging** requirements for automated and manual failover actions.\\n- Guardrails for **cross-region routing** by customer tier (especially Enterprise and regulated workloads).\\n\\nThis guidance is mandatory for:\\n- Smart routing and policy engine changes that can influence region selection.\\n- Failover automation controller behavior (including dry-run and simulation modes).\\n- On-call execution and controlled failover tests (\\\"game days\\\").\\n\\n## Scope / Non-scope\\n**In scope**\\n- Hosted API and Dedicated failover behavior across Redwood-managed regions.\\n- Data residency enforcement at routing and control-plane policy layers.\\n- Audit events, retention, and access control for failover decisioning.\\n\\n**Out of scope**\\n- Customer-specific Private deployment automation (see Private guidance). This doc provides patterns only.\\n- Changes to customer contracts/SLA language (handled separately).\\n\\n## Definitions\\n- **Region**: A cloud provider region (e.g., us-east, eu-west).\\n- **Residency boundary**: The allowed set of regions in which a tenant\\u2019s **inference data plane** traffic may be processed.\\n- **Data plane**: Prompts, model inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads processed by inference.\\n- **Control plane**: Tenant metadata, config, quotas, routing policy config, and operational telemetry.\\n- **Failover**: Automatic or operator-approved routing change that shifts traffic from a primary region to another region.\\n- **Enterprise tier**: Contracted customers with security requirements (auditability, residency, notification expectations).\\n\\n## Security principles (must-haves)\\n1) **Residency first**: If a tenant has a residency constraint, failover MUST stay within that boundary. Availability must be achieved *within* the allowed set; otherwise we prefer **graceful degradation** (e.g., 503 + Retry-After) over violating residency.\\n2) **Explicit allow-listing**: Cross-region routing must be controlled by explicit configuration per tenant (or per org) and audited.\\n3) **Least privilege and separation of duties**: Only designated on-call/SRE roles may initiate or approve production failover actions. Changes to residency boundaries require Security approval.\\n4) **Audit everything**: Every recommendation, execution, rollback, and override must emit a structured audit event with enough evidence to reconstruct \\u201cwho/what/why/when/impact.\\u201d\\n5) **Deterministic policy evaluation**: Given the same inputs, routing policy evaluation must produce the same output (to enable security review, auditability, and predictable enforcement).\\n\\n## Data residency policy\\n### Residency categories\\nRedwood supports the following residency categories for the **inference data plane** (prompts/outputs/embeddings):\\n\\n| Category | Description | Example allowed regions | Example prohibited regions |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| Global (no residency) | Tenant allows processing in any supported region | us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast | none |\\n| US-only | Processing restricted to US regions | us-east, us-west | eu-west |\\n| EU-only | Processing restricted to EU regions | eu-west, eu-central | us-east |\\n| Region-pinned | Processing restricted to a single region | eu-west only | all others |\\n| Custom boundary | Contract-defined set | (explicit per tenant) | all non-listed |\\n\\nNotes:\\n- Residency applies to **data plane processing**. Control-plane metadata may be replicated as needed for availability, but must follow the data classification and storage policies in Security standards.\\n- Region naming above is conceptual; the authoritative list is in routing config.\\n\\n### Default behavior by tier\\n- **Self-serve / Standard Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, unless the tenant explicitly configures otherwise.\\n- **Enterprise Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, but residency constraints may be contractually required (EU-only, US-only, or Custom boundary). These constraints MUST be encoded as enforceable routing policies.\\n- **Dedicated**: Default category follows the contracted deployment footprint. Failover is restricted to the customer\\u2019s approved Dedicated regions.\\n- **Private**: Residency enforcement is the customer\\u2019s responsibility, but Redwood-provided guidance should mirror the principles in this document.\\n\\n## Cross-region failover rules\\n### Hard rules (never violate)\\n1) **Do not route data plane traffic outside the tenant\\u2019s residency boundary.**\\n2) **Do not \\u201ctemporarily\\u201d violate residency to restore availability.** If no in-boundary failover target is healthy, degrade service within the boundary.\\n3) **Do not change residency boundaries during an incident** to work around a capacity/regional outage unless:\\n   - Approved by Security (delegate on-call) AND\\n   - Approved by the customer (if Enterprise/regulated) AND\\n   - Documented in an incident timeline with explicit timestamps and scope.\\n\\n### Allowed failover patterns\\n- **Within-boundary failover** (preferred):\\n  - EU-only: eu-west \\u2192 eu-central\\n  - US-only: us-east \\u2192 us-west\\n  - Custom: primary \\u2192 secondary (both explicitly allow-listed)\\n- **Region-pinned tenants**:\\n  - No cross-region failover. Use load shedding and communicate impairment.\\n\\n### Decision hierarchy interaction (security perspective)\\nRouting may decide to fail over due to reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, or capacity exhaustion; however:\\n- The policy engine MUST apply **residency gating as an absolute precondition** before evaluating \\u201cbest\\u201d region.\\n- If the \\u201cbest available\\u201d region is outside boundary, the decision must become **DEGRADE** (or keep traffic in-region with protective measures), not \\u201cfail over.\\u201d\\n\\n## Implementation requirements (routing, controller, and configs)\\n### Residency gating in the policy engine\\nThe policy engine must support a first-class predicate (conceptual):\\n- `allowed_regions(tenant_id)` returns a stable allow-list.\\n- Region selection must be `candidate_regions = healthy_regions \\u2229 allowed_regions`.\\n- If `candidate_regions` is empty, policy result must be one of:\\n  - `DEGRADE_WITHIN_BOUNDARY` (e.g., return 503/429 with Retry-After, reduce max tokens, disable optional features), or\\n  - `STAY_PUT_WITH_PROTECTION` (tight circuit breakers and load shedding), depending on product behavior.\\n\\nSecurity requirement: the code path must be **provably non-bypassable** (no \\u201cemergency override\\u201d without producing an audit event and requiring explicit approvals).\\n\\n### Configuration source of truth\\nFor Hosted and Dedicated:\\n- Residency boundary configuration must be stored in a **controlled configuration system** with:\\n  - Change review (required reviewers include Security for any boundary-tightening/loosening).\\n  - Immutable change history.\\n  - Rollback support.\\n\\n### Dedicated-specific constraints\\nDedicated customers may have:\\n- Hard region allow-lists bound to capacity pools.\\n- Explicit \\u201cno failover without approval\\u201d requirements.\\n\\nFailover automation for Dedicated must:\\n- Respect pool-level constraints (do not shift load to a pool not designated for that tenant).\\n- Coordinate with drain/evacuation procedures without exposing cross-tenant data.\\n\\n## Audit logging requirements\\n### What must be logged\\nAll systems participating in failover must emit structured events for:\\n- Recommendation (dry-run computation)\\n- Execution (policy flip applied)\\n- Rollback (automated or manual)\\n- Override (operator forcing a decision)\\n- Blocked action (attempted failover rejected due to residency boundary)\\n\\n### Required fields (minimum)\\nEach audit event must include (as applicable):\\n- **event_type**: recommend | execute | rollback | override | blocked\\n- **timestamp_utc**\\n- **tenant_id / org_id** (or an internal stable identifier)\\n- **tenant_tier**: self_serve | enterprise | dedicated\\n- **residency_category**: global | us_only | eu_only | region_pinned | custom\\n- **primary_region**, **target_region** (target may be empty for blocked/degrade)\\n- **decision**: failover | degrade | stay_put\\n- **reason_code**: reachability | error_burn | latency_burn | capacity | manual\\n- **evidence_refs**: links/IDs to region health snapshots, burn-rate alert IDs, probe runs\\n- **actor**: automation_controller | user:<id>\\n- **approval_state**: not_required | pending | approved | denied\\n- **change_id**: routing policy config revision / feature flag revision\\n- **correlation_ids**: incident_id (if any), request_id samples (optional), dashboard annotation ID\\n\\n### Retention and access\\n- Default retention (internal): **180 days** for audit events.\\n- Enterprise add-on / compliance packages: **\\u2265 400 days** retention, unless otherwise specified.\\n- Access must be restricted to:\\n  - SRE on-call and routing/control-plane engineers with an operational need\\n  - Security & compliance for audits and investigations\\n  - Customer Success only via approved exports/redactions (no raw prompt data)\\n\\n### Data minimization\\nAudit events must not include:\\n- Prompt text, model outputs, embeddings, or customer payloads.\\n- Customer secrets (API keys, tokens).\\n\\nIf request samples are needed for investigation, use approved secure logging mechanisms and follow incident response data handling procedures.\\n\\n## Handling of regulated / data-residency constrained customers\\n### If a region impairment occurs within a constrained boundary\\nExample: EU-only customer and eu-west is impaired.\\n- If eu-central is healthy and has capacity: **fail over to eu-central**.\\n- If no EU region is healthy/capable: **degrade within EU**.\\n  - Return 503 + Retry-After (preferred for overload)\\n  - Enforce stricter rate limits / max tokens for fairness\\n  - Disable non-essential optional features if supported by product policy\\n\\n### Communication expectations (Enterprise)\\n- During a real incident: follow the Regional Failover Communication Playbook.\\n- For planned tests: notify only customers whose traffic might be impacted, and explicitly state that residency boundaries will not be violated.\\n- If any customer perceives cross-region behavior, immediately:\\n  - Pull audit events for the tenant\\n  - Validate residency gating decisions\\n  - Engage Security and Support escalation\\n\\n## Controlled failover tests (\\u201cgame days\\u201d) security requirements\\nPrior to production tests:\\n1) Confirm residency gating is active and validated in staging.\\n2) Explicitly exclude region-pinned and regulated tenants unless written approval is obtained.\\n3) Ensure audit events and dashboard annotations are functioning.\\n4) Validate that \\u201cblocked due to residency\\u201d is observable (metric + audit event).\\n\\nDuring the test:\\n- Any attempted out-of-boundary action must be treated as a **SEV-2 security incident** if it results in data plane processing outside the boundary.\\n\\nAfter the test:\\n- Export the audit event summary for the test window and attach it to the game day results doc.\\n\\n## Operational checklist (on-call)\\nWhen failover automation suggests a policy change:\\n1) Identify tenant tier and residency category.\\n2) Confirm proposed target region is in allow-list.\\n3) Confirm automation approval requirements (some Enterprise/Dedicated tenants require ack).\\n4) Verify audit event emission is healthy (controller + policy engine).\\n5) Execute or approve.\\n6) If boundary prevents failover, choose degrade/stay-put path and update incident comms accordingly.\\n\\n## Examples\\n### Example A: Enterprise EU-only tenant during us-east incident\\n- Primary region: us-east (should not happen for EU-only; indicates misconfiguration)\\n- Required action:\\n  - Immediately block and correct routing policy (within incident change management)\\n  - File Security follow-up for residency misconfiguration\\n  - Confirm no data plane processing occurred outside EU via audit/telemetry\\n\\n### Example B: Global tenant during eu-west reachability failure\\n- Primary: eu-west\\n- Allowed: any region\\n- Action: fail over to us-east (or nearest healthy region by policy), emit audit events for recommend + execute + any rollback.\\n\\n### Example C: Region-pinned tenant when region is impaired\\n- Primary: eu-west\\n- Allowed: eu-west only\\n- Action: do not fail over. Enable protective controls (circuit breakers, load shedding), return Retry-After, and communicate impact.\\n\\n## Monitoring requirements (security-relevant)\\nMinimum dashboards/alerts needed:\\n- Count of `failover_blocked_due_to_residency` by tier\\n- Audit event delivery health (ingest lag, drop rate)\\n- Unauthorized/rare overrides (manual force actions)\\n- Drift detection: tenants with residency=EU-only receiving any non-EU routing decisions (should be zero)\\n\\n## Ownership and change control\\n- Owner: **Security & Compliance** (in partnership with SRE Reliability)\\n- Routing enforcement: **Smart Routing** team (Mina Haddad) + Policy engine owner (Jordan Lee)\\n- Audit event pipeline: **SRE / Observability** (Allison Grant)\\n\\nChanges to this document require review from:\\n- Security & Compliance\\n- SRE Reliability lead (Sean Gallagher or delegate)\\n- Routing policy tech lead (Ravi Menon)\\n\\n## Open questions / follow-ups\\n- Define a standard \\u201ccustom boundary\\u201d representation shared between Hosted and Dedicated policy configs.\\n- Confirm enterprise retention defaults for audit logs align with compliance add-ons.\\n- Add automated drift checks that continuously validate residency enforcement using synthetic tenant policies (no customer data).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349\"\n}",

document.title: Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)
document.content:
{
  "title": "Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)",
  "space": "security-and-compliance",
  "author": "Miles Thornton",
  "owner_team": "security",
  "status": "published",
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "created_at": "2026-01-07",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-12",
  "reviewers": [
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Mina Haddad",
    "Victor Alvarez",
    "Simran Kaur"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "security",
    "reliability",
    "failover",
    "data-residency",
    "routing",
    "audit-logging",
    "enterprise"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json",
    "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json"
  ],
  "content": "## Purpose
This document defines **security boundaries that must be preserved during regional failover** for Redwood Inference (Hosted API and Dedicated). It specifies:
- How **data residency constraints** restrict routing/failover.
- **Audit logging** requirements for automated and manual failover actions.
- Guardrails for **cross-region routing** by customer tier (especially Enterprise and regulated workloads).

This guidance is mandatory for:
- Smart routing and policy engine changes that can influence region selection.
- Failover automation controller behavior (including dry-run and simulation modes).
- On-call execution and controlled failover tests ("game days").

## Scope / Non-scope
**In scope**
- Hosted API and Dedicated failover behavior across Redwood-managed regions.
- Data residency enforcement at routing and control-plane policy layers.
- Audit events, retention, and access control for failover decisioning.

**Out of scope**
- Customer-specific Private deployment automation (see Private guidance). This doc provides patterns only.
- Changes to customer contracts/SLA language (handled separately).

## Definitions
- **Region**: A cloud provider region (e.g., us-east, eu-west).
- **Residency boundary**: The allowed set of regions in which a tenant’s **inference data plane** traffic may be processed.
- **Data plane**: Prompts, model inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads processed by inference.
- **Control plane**: Tenant metadata, config, quotas, routing policy config, and operational telemetry.
- **Failover**: Automatic or operator-approved routing change that shifts traffic from a primary region to another region.
- **Enterprise tier**: Contracted customers with security requirements (auditability, residency, notification expectations).

## Security principles (must-haves)
1) **Residency first**: If a tenant has a residency constraint, failover MUST stay within that boundary. Availability must be achieved *within* the allowed set; otherwise we prefer **graceful degradation** (e.g., 503 + Retry-After) over violating residency.
2) **Explicit allow-listing**: Cross-region routing must be controlled by explicit configuration per tenant (or per org) and audited.
3) **Least privilege and separation of duties**: Only designated on-call/SRE roles may initiate or approve production failover actions. Changes to residency boundaries require Security approval.
4) **Audit everything**: Every recommendation, execution, rollback, and override must emit a structured audit event with enough evidence to reconstruct “who/what/why/when/impact.”
5) **Deterministic policy evaluation**: Given the same inputs, routing policy evaluation must produce the same output (to enable security review, auditability, and predictable enforcement).

## Data residency policy
### Residency categories
Redwood supports the following residency categories for the **inference data plane** (prompts/outputs/embeddings):

| Category | Description | Example allowed regions | Example prohibited regions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Global (no residency) | Tenant allows processing in any supported region | us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast | none |
| US-only | Processing restricted to US regions | us-east, us-west | eu-west |
| EU-only | Processing restricted to EU regions | eu-west, eu-central | us-east |
| Region-pinned | Processing restricted to a single region | eu-west only | all others |
| Custom boundary | Contract-defined set | (explicit per tenant) | all non-listed |

Notes:
- Residency applies to **data plane processing**. Control-plane metadata may be replicated as needed for availability, but must follow the data classification and storage policies in Security standards.
- Region naming above is conceptual; the authoritative list is in routing config.

### Default behavior by tier
- **Self-serve / Standard Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, unless the tenant explicitly configures otherwise.
- **Enterprise Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, but residency constraints may be contractually required (EU-only, US-only, or Custom boundary). These constraints MUST be encoded as enforceable routing policies.
- **Dedicated**: Default category follows the contracted deployment footprint. Failover is restricted to the customer’s approved Dedicated regions.
- **Private**: Residency enforcement is the customer’s responsibility, but Redwood-provided guidance should mirror the principles in this document.

## Cross-region failover rules
### Hard rules (never violate)
1) **Do not route data plane traffic outside the tenant’s residency boundary.**
2) **Do not “temporarily” violate residency to restore availability.** If no in-boundary failover target is healthy, degrade service within the boundary.
3) **Do not change residency boundaries during an incident** to work around a capacity/regional outage unless:
   - Approved by Security (delegate on-call) AND
   - Approved by the customer (if Enterprise/regulated) AND
   - Documented in an incident timeline with explicit timestamps and scope.

### Allowed failover patterns
- **Within-boundary failover** (preferred):
  - EU-only: eu-west → eu-central
  - US-only: us-east → us-west
  - Custom: primary → secondary (both explicitly allow-listed)
- **Region-pinned tenants**:
  - No cross-region failover. Use load shedding and communicate impairment.

### Decision hierarchy interaction (security perspective)
Routing may decide to fail over due to reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, or capacity exhaustion; however:
- The policy engine MUST apply **residency gating as an absolute precondition** before evaluating “best” region.
- If the “best available” region is outside boundary, the decision must become **DEGRADE** (or keep traffic in-region with protective measures), not “fail over.”

## Implementation requirements (routing, controller, and configs)
### Residency gating in the policy engine
The policy engine must support a first-class predicate (conceptual):
- `allowed_regions(tenant_id)` returns a stable allow-list.
- Region selection must be `candidate_regions = healthy_regions ∩ allowed_regions`.
- If `candidate_regions` is empty, policy result must be one of:
  - `DEGRADE_WITHIN_BOUNDARY` (e.g., return 503/429 with Retry-After, reduce max tokens, disable optional features), or
  - `STAY_PUT_WITH_PROTECTION` (tight circuit breakers and load shedding), depending on product behavior.

Security requirement: the code path must be **provably non-bypassable** (no “emergency override” without producing an audit event and requiring explicit approvals).

### Configuration source of truth
For Hosted and Dedicated:
- Residency boundary configuration must be stored in a **controlled configuration system** with:
  - Change review (required reviewers include Security for any boundary-tightening/loosening).
  - Immutable change history.
  - Rollback support.

### Dedicated-specific constraints
Dedicated customers may have:
- Hard region allow-lists bound to capacity pools.
- Explicit “no failover without approval” requirements.

Failover automation for Dedicated must:
- Respect pool-level constraints (do not shift load to a pool not designated for that tenant).
- Coordinate with drain/evacuation procedures without exposing cross-tenant data.

## Audit logging requirements
### What must be logged
All systems participating in failover must emit structured events for:
- Recommendation (dry-run computation)
- Execution (policy flip applied)
- Rollback (automated or manual)
- Override (operator forcing a decision)
- Blocked action (attempted failover rejected due to residency boundary)

### Required fields (minimum)
Each audit event must include (as applicable):
- **event_type**: recommend | execute | rollback | override | blocked
- **timestamp_utc**
- **tenant_id / org_id** (or an internal stable identifier)
- **tenant_tier**: self_serve | enterprise | dedicated
- **residency_category**: global | us_only | eu_only | region_pinned | custom
- **primary_region**, **target_region** (target may be empty for blocked/degrade)
- **decision**: failover | degrade | stay_put
- **reason_code**: reachability | error_burn | latency_burn | capacity | manual
- **evidence_refs**: links/IDs to region health snapshots, burn-rate alert IDs, probe runs
- **actor**: automation_controller | user:<id>
- **approval_state**: not_required | pending | approved | denied
- **change_id**: routing policy config revision / feature flag revision
- **correlation_ids**: incident_id (if any), request_id samples (optional), dashboard annotation ID

### Retention and access
- Default retention (internal): **180 days** for audit events.
- Enterprise add-on / compliance packages: **≥ 400 days** retention, unless otherwise specified.
- Access must be restricted to:
  - SRE on-call and routing/control-plane engineers with an operational need
  - Security & compliance for audits and investigations
  - Customer Success only via approved exports/redactions (no raw prompt data)

### Data minimization
Audit events must not include:
- Prompt text, model outputs, embeddings, or customer payloads.
- Customer secrets (API keys, tokens).

If request samples are needed for investigation, use approved secure logging mechanisms and follow incident response data handling procedures.

## Handling of regulated / data-residency constrained customers
### If a region impairment occurs within a constrained boundary
Example: EU-only customer and eu-west is impaired.
- If eu-central is healthy and has capacity: **fail over to eu-central**.
- If no EU region is healthy/capable: **degrade within EU**.
  - Return 503 + Retry-After (preferred for overload)
  - Enforce stricter rate limits / max tokens for fairness
  - Disable non-essential optional features if supported by product policy

### Communication expectations (Enterprise)
- During a real incident: follow the Regional Failover Communication Playbook.
- For planned tests: notify only customers whose traffic might be impacted, and explicitly state that residency boundaries will not be violated.
- If any customer perceives cross-region behavior, immediately:
  - Pull audit events for the tenant
  - Validate residency gating decisions
  - Engage Security and Support escalation

## Controlled failover tests (“game days”) security requirements
Prior to production tests:
1) Confirm residency gating is active and validated in staging.
2) Explicitly exclude region-pinned and regulated tenants unless written approval is obtained.
3) Ensure audit events and dashboard annotations are functioning.
4) Validate that “blocked due to residency” is observable (metric + audit event).

During the test:
- Any attempted out-of-boundary action must be treated as a **SEV-2 security incident** if it results in data plane processing outside the boundary.

After the test:
- Export the audit event summary for the test window and attach it to the game day results doc.

## Operational checklist (on-call)
When failover automation suggests a policy change:
1) Identify tenant tier and residency category.
2) Confirm proposed target region is in allow-list.
3) Confirm automation approval requirements (some Enterprise/Dedicated tenants require ack).
4) Verify audit event emission is healthy (controller + policy engine).
5) Execute or approve.
6) If boundary prevents failover, choose degrade/stay-put path and update incident comms accordingly.

## Examples
### Example A: Enterprise EU-only tenant during us-east incident
- Primary region: us-east (should not happen for EU-only; indicates misconfiguration)
- Required action:
  - Immediately block and correct routing policy (within incident change management)
  - File Security follow-up for residency misconfiguration
  - Confirm no data plane processing occurred outside EU via audit/telemetry

### Example B: Global tenant during eu-west reachability failure
- Primary: eu-west
- Allowed: any region
- Action: fail over to us-east (or nearest healthy region by policy), emit audit events for recommend + execute + any rollback.

### Example C: Region-pinned tenant when region is impaired
- Primary: eu-west
- Allowed: eu-west only
- Action: do not fail over. Enable protective controls (circuit breakers, load shedding), return Retry-After, and communicate impact.

## Monitoring requirements (security-relevant)
Minimum dashboards/alerts needed:
- Count of `failover_blocked_due_to_residency` by tier
- Audit event delivery health (ingest lag, drop rate)
- Unauthorized/rare overrides (manual force actions)
- Drift detection: tenants with residency=EU-only receiving any non-EU routing decisions (should be zero)

## Ownership and change control
- Owner: **Security & Compliance** (in partnership with SRE Reliability)
- Routing enforcement: **Smart Routing** team (Mina Haddad) + Policy engine owner (Jordan Lee)
- Audit event pipeline: **SRE / Observability** (Allison Grant)

Changes to this document require review from:
- Security & Compliance
- SRE Reliability lead (Sean Gallagher or delegate)
- Routing policy tech lead (Ravi Menon)

## Open questions / follow-ups
- Define a standard “custom boundary” representation shared between Hosted and Dedicated policy configs.
- Confirm enterprise retention defaults for audit logs align with compliance add-ons.
- Add automated drift checks that continuously validate residency enforcement using synthetic tenant policies (no customer data).

# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency

**Audience:** Support  
**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Status:** Corrected canonical policy  
**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Signed customer terms override this general guidance.

## Support-facing rule

### Default retention

| Data class | Default or commitment |
|---|---|
| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |
| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |
| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |
| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |

These defaults come from the published retention policy. Do not replace them with customer questionnaire values unless the customer's signed terms or account configuration establish different settings.

### Verified erasure or tenant termination

- After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days.
- Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days.
- A deletion attestation is available on request after completion. Support must describe its scope precisely; a primary-store completion notice is not evidence that backup scrub has completed.
- The stronger evidence says termination marks tenant data for purge and serving stops immediately. Support must still validate authorization and the applicable contract before initiating the workflow.

### Residency and cross-region behavior

- Hosted inference data-plane traffic must remain within an enforced tenant residency boundary. If no allowed region is available, service degrades rather than routing outside the boundary.
- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA.
- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.
- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.

## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions

- The evidence does not establish that every non-EU residency configuration automatically restricts backup geography; validate the contract and backup configuration.
- The evidence does not establish a universal location for all control-plane metadata.
- The 90-day backup statement must not be presented as overriding a legal hold, regulatory constraint, or contractually extended retention. Escalate those cases.
- The published tenant decommission certification playbook is scoped to Dedicated and Private, not Hosted API. Its 10-business-day operational SLA must not be quoted for Hosted.
- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window remains unresolved because the sources conflict (180, 365, and other values in different contexts). Do not infer it from request-log retention.
- Customer-specific accelerated deletion terms and retention extensions apply only when signed and verified.

## Validation before answering a customer

1. Confirm Hosted API deployment, tenant ID, authorized requester, and whether the request is erasure, termination, or both.
2. Check signed retention/residency terms, legal or regulatory holds, account-level logging configuration, backup retention, and DR replication settings.
3. Inventory the requested data classes and distinguish primary-store completion from backup/snapshot completion.
4. For residency, confirm the enforced data-plane boundary separately from backup and control-plane settings.
5. Do not issue final-completion language until the deletion attestation covers the promised scope. Record the ticket, timestamps, affected artifact classes, and attestation reference.
6. Escalate conflicts or missing configuration evidence to Security/Privacy and SRE.

## Evidence

- [Customer data + logs retention policy (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-data-and-logs-retention-policy.json) — `dsid_e51021765c694a65bd60b3d38b12db6e`
- [Data retention and deletion (Security FAQ excerpt)](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/data-retention-and-deletion-faq.json) — `dsid_b6fb2620d47d44e3b17b16b42f1e021f`
- [Hosted API: Data geography, TTL & purge cadence — security questionnaire responses](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) — `dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`
- [Hosted Data Residency Policy and Engineering Controls](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/hosted-data-residency-policy-and-controls.json) — `dsid_eb9f7314dd10443fbf70a80306d5119a`
- [Failover and Security Boundaries](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json) — `dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349`
- [Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/tenant-decommission-and-data-erase-certification-playbook-2026.json) — `dsid_c7f6ff2dcf674dd784e7f65c738d0724` (scope limitation only)

# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency

**Audience:** Support  
**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Status:** Corrected canonical policy  
**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Signed customer terms override this general guidance.

## Support-facing rule

### Default retention

| Data class | Default or commitment |
|---|---|
| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |
| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |
| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |
| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |

These defaults come from the published retention policy. Do not replace them with customer questionnaire values unless the customer's signed terms or account configuration establish different settings.

### Verified erasure or tenant termination

- After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days.
- Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days.
- A deletion attestation is available on request after completion. Support must describe its scope precisely; a primary-store completion notice is not evidence that backup scrub has completed.
- The stronger evidence says termination marks tenant data for purge and serving stops immediately. Support must still validate authorization and the applicable contract before initiating the workflow.

### Residency and cross-region behavior

- Hosted inference data-plane traffic must remain within an enforced tenant residency boundary. If no allowed region is available, service degrades rather than routing outside the boundary.
- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA.
- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.
- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.

## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions",

# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency

**Audience:** Support  
**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Status:** Corrected canonical policy  
**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Signed customer terms override this general guidance.

## Support-facing rule

### Default retention

| Data class | Default or commitment |
|---|---|
| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |
| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |
| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |
| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |

These defaults come from the published retention policy. Do not replace them with customer questionnaire values unless the customer's signed terms or account configuration establish different settings.

### Verified erasure or tenant termination

- After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days.
- Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days.
- A deletion attestation is available on request after completion. Support must describe its scope precisely; a primary-store completion notice is not evidence that backup scrub has completed.
- The stronger evidence says termination marks tenant data for purge and serving stops immediately. Support must still validate authorization and the applicable contract before initiating the workflow.

### Residency and cross-region behavior

- Hosted inference data-plane traffic must remain within an enforced tenant residency boundary. If no allowed region is available, service degrades rather than routing outside the boundary.
- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA.
- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.
- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.

## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions
