              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention rule (baseline)\nSource: agent-memory\nPath: /memory/semantic_memory/hosted-api-retention-rule-baseline-ntion_v1.md\nWorkspace: agent-memory\nTeam: Ethan Park\n\n# Hosted API retention rule (baseline)\n\nMemory type: semantic_memory\nRecorded: 2026-08-14T17:21:57.575303+00:00\nConfidence: 0.88\nOwner: Ethan Park\nTags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, support\n\n## Summary\n\nFor Redwood-managed Hosted API, customer prompts/outputs are not persistently stored by default; explicitly enabled debug payload logging is retained 7 days; metadata-only operational request logs and no-payload traces are retained 14 days; verified deletion requests for stored data in Redwood-managed systems complete within 30 days.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency (corrected)\nSource: agent-memory\nPath: /memory/semantic_memory/hosted-api-retention-deletion-and-residency-corrected-ntion_v2.md\nWorkspace: agent-memory\nTeam: Ethan Park\n\n# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency (corrected)\n\nMemory type: semantic_memory\nRecorded: 2026-08-14T17:23:36.714993+00:00\nConfidence: 0.93\nOwner: Ethan Park\nTags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, corrected\n\n## Summary\n\nCorrected support rule: Hosted customer content is not persistently stored by default; enabled debug payloads retain 7 days and metadata-only request logs/no-payload traces retain 14 days. After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days and backups/replicated snapshots within 90 days; an attestation is available after completion and must be scoped to the completed stage. Hosted inference data-plane traffic stays within an enforced residency boundary, but backups may replicate for DR depending on SLA; EU-only enterprise terms disable cross-region backup replication. Do not promise universal control-plane locality, a Hosted 10-business-day certification SLA, unconditional timelines despite holds/contracts, or a general audit-log window.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\n- dsid_e51021765c694a65bd60b3d38b12db6e\n- dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3\n- dsid_eb9f7314dd10443fbf70a80306d5119a\n- dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349\n- dsid_c7f6ff2dcf674dd784e7f65c738d0724\n\n## Supersedes\n\n- mem_hosted_api_retention_v1",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention and deletion\nSource: Ethan Park / Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-hosted-api-retention-v1\n\n# Hosted API retention and deletion\n\n**Audience:** Support  \n**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  \n**Status:** Published baseline  \n**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Contract-specific terms override this general guidance.\n\n## Support-facing rule\n\n| Data class | Default or commitment |\n|---|---|\n| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |\n| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |\n| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n| Stored data covered by a verified deletion request | Redwood completes deletion from Redwood-managed systems within 30 days of verification. |\n\nSupport must not describe the 30-day deletion statement as proof of backup erasure or tenant-termination cleanup. The available baseline evidence does not establish those behaviors.\n\n## Explicit unknowns\n\n- Whether tenant termination automatically starts a tenant-wide erasure workflow.\n- Whether any backup or snapshot may contain Hosted API customer data, and the maximum time until such copies are irrecoverable.\n- Whether a deletion confirmation includes backup purge evidence.\n- Whether region pinning covers backups, disaster-recovery replicas, and all control-plane metadata.\n- Whether legal holds or contract-specific exceptions alter deletion timing.\n- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window; this policy does not infer it from request-log retention.\n\n## Validation before answering a customer\n\n1. Confirm the deployment is Hosted API and identify any contract-specific retention or residency terms.\n2. Confirm whether debug payload logging is enabled for the organization.\n3. For deletion, verify the request and identify each targeted data class; open the approved deletion workflow.\n4. Escalate questions about backups, tenant termination, certificates, legal holds, or cross-region copies to Security/Privacy and SRE. Do not promise a completion window until written evidence covers the requested scope.\n5. Cite the applicable source and record the customer-specific answer in the support ticket.\n\n## Evidence",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency\nSource: Ethan Park / Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-hosted-api-retention-correction\n\n# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency\n\n**Audience:** Support  \n**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  \n**Status:** Corrected canonical policy  \n**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Signed customer terms override this general guidance.\n\n## Support-facing rule\n\n### Default retention\n\n| Data class | Default or commitment |\n|---|---|\n| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |\n| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |\n| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n\nThese defaults come from the published retention policy. Do not replace them with customer questionnaire values unless the customer's signed terms or account configuration establish different settings.\n\n### Verified erasure or tenant termination\n\n- After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days.\n- Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days.\n- A deletion attestation is available on request after completion. Support must describe its scope precisely; a primary-store completion notice is not evidence that backup scrub has completed.\n- The stronger evidence says termination marks tenant data for purge and serving stops immediately. Support must still validate authorization and the applicable contract before initiating the workflow.\n\n### Residency and cross-region behavior\n\n- Hosted inference data-plane traffic must remain within an enforced tenant residency boundary. If no allowed region is available, service degrades rather than routing outside the boundary.\n- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA.\n- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.\n- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.\n\n## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions",

              "ordinal": 1,
              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency\nSource: Ethan Park / Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-hosted-api-retention-correction\n\nA.\n- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.\n- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.\n\n## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions\n\n- The evidence does not establish that every non-EU residency configuration automatically restricts backup geography; validate the contract and backup configuration.\n- The evidence does not establish a universal location for all control-plane metadata.\n- The 90-day backup statement must not be presented as overriding a legal hold, regulatory constraint, or contractually extended retention. Escalate those cases.\n- The published tenant decommission certification playbook is scoped to Dedicated and Private, not Hosted API. Its 10-business-day operational SLA must not be quoted for Hosted.\n- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window remains unresolved because the sources conflict (180, 365, and other values in different contexts). Do not infer it from request-log retention.\n- Customer-specific accelerated deletion terms and retention extensions apply only when signed and verified.\n\n## Validation before answering a customer\n\n1. Confirm Hosted API deployment, tenant ID, authorized requester, and whether the request is erasure, termination, or both.\n2. Check signed retention/residency terms, legal or regulatory holds, account-level logging configuration, backup retention, and DR replication settings.\n3. Inventory the requested data classes and distinguish primary-store completion from backup/snapshot completion.\n4. For residency, confirm the enforced data-plane boundary separately from backup and control-plane settings.\n5. Do not issue final-completion language until the deletion attestation covers the promised scope. Record the ticket, timestamps, affected artifact classes, and attestation reference.\n6. Escalate conflicts or missing configuration evidence to Security/Privacy and SRE.\n\n## Evidence",

            "content": "# Hosted API retention and deletion\n\n**Audience:** Support  \n**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  \n**Status:** Published baseline  \n**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Contract-specific terms override this general guidance.\n\n## Support-facing rule\n\n| Data class | Default or commitment |\n|---|---|\n| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |\n| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |\n| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n| Stored data covered by a verified deletion request | Redwood completes deletion from Redwood-managed systems within 30 days of verification. |\n\nSupport must not describe the 30-day deletion statement as proof of backup erasure or tenant-termination cleanup.             "content": "# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency\n\n**Audience:** Support  \n**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  \n**Status:** Corrected canonical policy  \n**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Signed customer terms override this general guidance.\n\n## Support-facing rule\n\n### Default retention\n\n| Data class | Default or commitment |\n|---|---|\n| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |\n| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |\n| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n\nThese defaults come from the published retention policy. Do not replace them with customer questionnaire values unless the customer's signed terms or account configuration establish different settings.\n\n### Verified erasure or tenant termination\n\n- After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days.\n- Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days.\n- A deletion attestation is available on request after completion. Support must describe its scope precisely; a primary-store completion notice is not evidence that backup scrub has completed.\n- The stronger evidence says termination marks tenant data for purge and serving stops immediately. Support must still validate authorization and the applicable contract before initiating the workflow.\n\n### Residency and cross-region behavior\n\n- Hosted inference data-plane traffic must remain within an enforced tenant residency boundary. If no allowed region is available, service degrades rather than routing outside the boundary.\n- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA.\n- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.\n- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.\n\n## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions\n\n- The evidence does not establish that every non-EU residency configuration automatically restricts backup geography; validate the contract and backup configuration.\n- The evidence does not establish a universal location for all control-plane metadata.\n- The 90-day backup statement must not be presented as overriding a legal hold, regulatory constraint, or contractually extended retention. Escalate those cases.\n- The published tenant decommission certification playbook is scoped to Dedicated and Private, not Hosted API. Its 10-business-day operational SLA must not be quoted for Hosted.\n- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window remains unresolved because the sources conflict (180, 365, and other values in different contexts). Do not infer it from request-log retention.\n- Customer-specific accelerated deletion terms and retention extensions apply only when signed and verified.\n\n## Validation before answering a customer\n\n1. Confirm Hosted API deployment, tenant ID, authorized requester, and whether the request is erasure, termination, or both.\n2. Check signed retention/residency terms, legal or regulatory holds, account-level logging configuration, backup retention, and DR replication settings.\n3. Inventory the requested data classes and distinguish primary-store completion from backup/snapshot completion.\n4. For residency, confirm the enforced data-plane boundary separately from backup and control-plane settings.\n5. Do not issue final-completion language until the deletion attestation covers the promised scope. Record the ticket, timestamps, affected artifact classes, and attestation reference.\n6. Escalate conflicts or missing configuration evidence to Security/Privacy and SRE.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- [Customer data + logs retention policy (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-reside",

# Hosted API retention and deletion

**Audience:** Support  
**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Status:** Published baseline  
**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Contract-specific terms override this general guidance.

## Support-facing rule

| Data class | Default or commitment |
|---|---|
| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |
| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |
| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |
| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |
| Stored data covered by a verified deletion request | Redwood completes deletion from Redwood-managed systems within 30 days of verification. |

Support must not describe the 30-day deletion statement as proof of backup erasure or tenant-termination cleanup. The available baseline evidence does not establish those behaviors.

## Explicit unknowns

- Whether tenant termination automatically starts a tenant-wide erasure workflow.
- Whether any backup or snapshot may contain Hosted API customer data, and the maximum time until such copies are irrecoverable.
- Whether a deletion confirmation includes backup purge evidence.
- Whether region pinning covers backups, disaster-recovery replicas, and all control-plane metadata.
- Whether legal holds or contract-specific exceptions alter deletion timing.
- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window; this policy does not infer it from request-log retention.

## Validation before answering a customer

1. Confirm the deployment is Hosted API and identify any contract-specific retention or residency terms.
2. Confirm whether debug payload logging is enabled for the organization.
3. For deletion, verify the request and identify each targeted data class; open the approved deletion workflow.
4. Escalate questions about backups, tenant termination, certificates, legal holds, or cross-region copies to Security/Privacy and SRE. Do not promise a completion window until written evidence covers the requested scope.
5. Cite the applicable source and record the customer-specific answer in the support ticket.

- After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days.
- Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days.
- A deletion attestation is available on request after completion. Support must describe its scope precisely; a primary-store completion notice is not evidence that backup scrub has completed.

- Hosted inference data-plane traffic must remain within an enforced tenant residency boundary. If no allowed region is available, service degrades rather than routing outside the boundary.
- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA.
- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.
- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.

Tags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, corrected

## Summary

Corrected support rule: Hosted customer content is not persistently stored by default; enabled debug payloads retain 7 days and metadata-only request logs/no-payload traces retain 14 days. After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days and backups/replicated snapshots within 90 days; an attestation is available after completion and must be scoped to the completed stage. Hosted inference data-plane traffic stays within an enforced residency boundary, but backups may replicate for DR depending on SLA; EU-only enterprise terms disable cross-region backup replication. Do not promise universal control-plane locality, a Hosted 10-business-day certification SLA, unconditional timelines despite holds/contracts, or a general audit-log window.

Signed customer terms override this general guidance.\n\n## Support-facing rule\n\n### Default retention\n\n| Data class | Default or commitment |\n|---|---|\n| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |\n| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |\n| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |\n\nThese defaults come from the published retention policy. Do not replace them with customer questionnaire values unless the customer's signed terms or account configuration establish different settings.\n\n### Verified erasure or tenant termination\n\n- After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days.\n- Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days.\n- A deletion attestation is available on request after completion. Support must describe its scope precisely; a primary-store completion notice is not evidence that backup scrub has completed.\n- The stronger evidence says termination marks tenant data for purge and serving stops immediately. Support must still validate authorization and the applicable contract before initiating the workflow.\n\n### Residency and cross-region behavior\n\n- Hosted inference data-plane traffic must remain within an enforced tenant residency boundary. If no allowed region is available, service degrades rather than routing outside the boundary.\n- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA.\n- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.\n- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.\n\n## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions\n\n- The evidence does not establish that every non-EU residency configuration automatically restricts backup geography; validate the contract and backup configuration.\n- The evidence does not establish a universal location for all control-plane metadata.\n- The 90-day backup statement must not be presented as overriding a legal hold, regulatory constraint, or contractually extended retention. Escalate those cases.\n- The published tenant decommission certification playbook is scoped to Dedicated and Private, not Hosted API. Its 10-business-day operational SLA must not be quoted for Hosted.\n- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window remains unresolved because the sources conflict (180, 365, and other values in different contexts). document.content:
# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency

**Audience:** Support  
**Owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Status:** Corrected canonical policy  
**Scope:** Redwood-managed Hosted API. Signed customer terms override this general guidance.

## Support-facing rule

### Default retention

| Data class | Default or commitment |
|---|---|
| Customer content (prompts and outputs) | Not stored persistently by default. |
| Debug payload logging | Stored only when explicitly enabled for an organization; retained for 7 days. |
| Operational request logs | Metadata only, not payloads; retained for 14 days. |
| Tracing spans | Linked to request IDs and contain no payloads; retained for 14 days. |

These defaults come from the published retention policy. Do not replace them with customer questionnaire values unless the customer's signed terms or account configuration establish different settings.

### Verified erasure or tenant termination

- After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days.
- Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days.
- A deletion attestation is available on request after completion. Support must describe its scope precisely; a primary-store completion notice is not evidence that backup scrub has completed.
- The stronger evidence says termination marks tenant data for purge and serving stops immediately. Support must still validate authorization and the applicable contract before initiating the workflow.

### Residency and cross-region behavior

- Hosted inference data-plane traffic must remain within an enforced tenant residency boundary. If no allowed region is available, service degrades rather than routing outside the boundary.
- Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA.
- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.
- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.

## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions

- The evidence does not establish that every non-EU residency configuration automatically restricts backup geography; validate the contract and backup configuration.
- The evidence does not establish a universal location for all control-plane metadata.
- The 90-day backup statement must not be presented as overriding a legal hold, regulatory constraint, or contractually extended retention. Escalate those cases.
- The published tenant decommission certification playbook is scoped to Dedicated and Private, not Hosted API. Its 10-business-day operational SLA must not be quoted for Hosted.
- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window remains unresolved because the sources conflict (180, 365, and other values in different contexts). Do not infer it from request-log retention.
- Customer-specific accelerated deletion terms and retention extensions apply only when signed and verified.

## Validation before answering a customer

1. Confirm Hosted API deployment, tenant ID, authorized requester, and whether the request is erasure, termination, or both.
2. Check signed retention/residency terms, legal or regulatory holds, account-level logging configuration, backup retention, and DR replication settings.
3. Inventory the requested data classes and distinguish primary-store completion from backup/snapshot completion.
4. For residency, confirm the enforced data-plane boundary separately from backup and control-plane settings.
5. Do not issue final-completion language until the deletion attestation covers the promised scope. Record the ticket, timestamps, affected artifact classes, and attestation reference.
6. Escalate conflicts or missing configuration evidence to Security/Privacy and SRE.

## Evidence

- [Hosted API: Data geography, TTL & purge cadence — security questionnaire responses](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) — `dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`

# Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency (corrected)

Memory type: semantic_memory
Recorded: 2026-08-14T17:23:36.714993+00:00

Owner: Ethan Park
Tags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, corrected

## Summary

Corrected support rule: Hosted customer content is not persistently stored by default; enabled debug payloads retain 7 days and metadata-only request logs/no-payload traces retain 14 days. After a verified erasure request or tenant termination, primary data is purged within 30 days and backups/replicated snapshots within 90 days; an attestation is available after completion and must be scoped to the completed stage. Hosted inference data-plane traffic stays within an enforced residency boundary, but backups may replicate for DR depending on SLA; EU-only enterprise terms disable cross-region backup replication. Do not promise universal control-plane locality, a Hosted 10-business-day certification SLA, unconditional timelines despite holds/contracts, or a general audit-log window.

  "text": "[Document context]
Title: Hosted API retention, deletion, and residency
Source: Ethan Park / Platform & Console
Path: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md
Workspace: task/ethan-hosted-api-retention-correction

A.
- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.
- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.

## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions

- The evidence does not establish that every non-EU residency configuration automatically restricts backup geography; validate the contract and backup configuration.
- The evidence does not establish a universal location for all control-plane metadata.
- The 90-day backup statement must not be presented as overriding a legal hold, regulatory constraint, or contractually extended retention. Escalate those cases.
- The published tenant decommission certification playbook is scoped to Dedicated and Private, not Hosted API. Its 10-business-day operational SLA must not be quoted for Hosted.
- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window remains unresolved because the sources conflict (180, 365, and other values in different contexts). Do not infer it from request-log retention.
- Customer-specific accelerated deletion terms and retention extensions apply only when signed and verified.

## Validation before answering a customer

1. Confirm Hosted API deployment, tenant ID, authorized requester, and whether the request is erasure, termination, or both.
2. Check signed retention/residency terms, legal or regulatory holds, account-level logging configuration, backup retention, and DR replication settings.
3. Inventory the requested data classes and distinguish primary-store completion from backup/snapshot completion.
4. For residency, confirm the enforced data-plane boundary separately from backup and control-plane settings.
5. Do not issue final-completion language until the deletion attestation covers the promised scope. Record the ticket, timestamps, affected artifact classes, and attestation reference.
6. Escalate conflicts or missing configuration evidence to Security/Privacy and SRE.

## Evidence",

A.
- For an EU-only enterprise contract, backup cross-region replication is disabled and backups remain within the contracted boundary.
- Do not promise that general region pinning covers every control-plane record. Published failover controls say control-plane metadata may be replicated under separate classification and storage policies.

## Preserved uncertainty and exceptions

- The evidence does not establish that every non-EU residency configuration automatically restricts backup geography; validate the contract and backup configuration.
- The evidence does not establish a universal location for all control-plane metadata.
- The 90-day backup statement must not be presented as overriding a legal hold, regulatory constraint, or contractually extended retention. Escalate those cases.
- The published tenant decommission certification playbook is scoped to Dedicated and Private, not Hosted API. Its 10-business-day operational SLA must not be quoted for Hosted.
- The general Hosted API audit-log retention window remains unresolved because the sources conflict (180, 365, and other values in different contexts). Do not infer it from request-log retention.
- Customer-specific accelerated deletion terms and retention extensions apply only when signed and verified.

## Validation before answering a customer

1. Confirm Hosted API deployment, tenant ID, authorized requester, and whether the request is erasure, termination, or both.
2. Check signed retention/residency terms, legal or regulatory holds, account-level logging configuration, backup retention, and DR replication settings.
3. Inventory the requested data classes and distinguish primary-store completion from backup/snapshot completion.
4. For residency, confirm the enforced data-plane boundary separately from backup and control-plane settings.
5. Do not issue final-completion language until the deletion attestation covers the promised scope. Record the ticket, timestamps, affected artifact classes, and attestation reference.
6. Escalate conflicts or missing configuration evidence to Security/Privacy and SRE.
